title: Earl of Elgin confirms James Bruce was a Freemason
place_text: Broomhall estate, Scotland; Canongate Kilwinning Lodge No. 2, Edinburgh

tellings.quote: dear boy of course he was a freebies and he gave me the lodge the kill winning lodge number two in Edinburgh that James Bruce was a member of

plain: The writer Graham Hancock says that in 1990, at the Broomhall estate in Scotland, the Earl of Elgin told him that the eighteenth-century Scottish traveller James Bruce was a Freemason, a member of the old secret brotherhood with its own rites: "dear boy, of course he was." Hancock says the Earl even named the lodge, Canongate Kilwinning Lodge No. 2 in Edinburgh, which Bruce belonged to. Hancock tells it as something he took part in while researching his book The Sign and the Seal, and it mattered to him because it tied Bruce's travels to the Freemasons.
